TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALLIE_000_264: Then everything can go back to the way it was...
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_REX_000_265: So he found you two shivering on the roadside when he was going through Werlyt. Lucky for you, eh?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALFONSE_000_266: If he hadn't, we'd probably be dead by now.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_REX_000_267: As for us three, our parents all died in the epidemic. We'd still be begging on street corners if it weren't for him.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALFONSE_000_268: I just wish there was a way we could repay Lord Gaius for all the kindness he's shown us.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_MILISANDIA_000_269: He fights for the Empire, so we should, too! That'll make him proud of us.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALFONSE_000_270: You're saying we should join the army?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_RICON_000_271: I don't think that's such a good idea... Everyone in Werlyt was scared of the Garleans. Why would we want to be like them?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALFONSE_000_272: Lord Gaius is different. I know he is.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_REX_000_273: You're right. He always says that the strong should lead the weak. Maybe that's why he took us in.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALFONSE_000_274: All right. If becoming a soldier is what it takes, I'll do it. Who's with me?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_REX_000_275: Count me in! And maybe one day, people'll look up to us like we do Lord Gaius.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALFONSE_000_276: Then it's settled. From now on, we're all brothers and sisters fighting for the same cause.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALLIE_000_277: Brothers and sisters? Then that would make Lord Gaius our...father?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALFONSE_000_278: Well, if he doesn't mind us calling him that, I suppose so.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_REX_000_279: And that makes you our big brother, since you're the oldest! You'd better be nice to us, or I'm telling Father. Ha ha!
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALLIE_000_280: Father... Since you went away, a lot has changed in the Empire. For us, too.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALLIE_000_281: If we'd known that you were still out there, still alive, none of this would've happened!
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SHADOWHUNTER_000_28: If you must go, I will not stop you, but answer me this: who was piloting the Ruby Weapon? We all know that Nael van Darnus has not returned from the dead.
No... No, I refuse to believe that.
I refuse to believe you would let that happen. She was a sister to you! To all of you!
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALFONSE_000_289: We only want to finish what you started.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALFONSE_000_290: And while we will never forget all you have done for us, the next time we meet, it shall be as enemies. Good-bye, Father.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_REX_000_291: As for you, hero of Eorzea, you'll pay for what you did to Milisandia. I swear it.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_301: Well, well. Gaius van Baelsar. We meet again.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_302: Come to see how your precious Weapon project has been proceeding in your absence, have you?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SHADOWHUNTER_000_30: You are come to collect data on the Ruby Weapon, correct? The pilot...Milisandia should still be inside the cockpit. I will ask Valdeaulin to escort you to the wreckage.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_304: Any idea who this Milisandia is? An imperial crony of his, perhaps?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_306: Gaius always did have an eye for talent and a mind to nurture it. In fact, Livia sas Junius was another protégé of his.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_307: He even took me under his wing when my father became obsessed with the Meteor project. It's strange that I felt closer to Gaius than my own flesh and blood.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_308: Then, my father and countless others lost their lives in the Bozja incident. Although he was acting under Emperor Solus's orders, he masterminded the whole thing.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_309: I'd begged him to reconsider, to put an end to this madness, but my words fell on deaf ears. That's when I turned to Gaius for support, but he was as much a pawn of the Emperor as my father, and refused to intervene. And when my turn came to serve, I defected and fled to Eorzea.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_310: I blamed Gaius as much as any of them, perhaps even more, for the barbaric acts carried out in the name of conquest. But when we met at the Praetorium, all the hatred that had been festering inside me seemed to fade away, and I remembered the man I once respected.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_311: To think the dreaded Black Wolf was a mere plaything of the Ascians, who left him broken and disgraced, having sent thousands of his men to early graves. It's more than most could bear. And now the lives of the children he raised hang in the balance.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_312: Any personal grievances I have with Gaius can wait. I'd best gather what information I can on the Ruby Weapon, but I'll be back as soon as possible.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_VALDEAULIN_000_315: Gaius wasn't exaggerating when he spoke of your prowess in battle. Unfortunately, it seems a fair few problems remain, and unlike the Ruby Weapon, it might take more than brute force to solve them.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SEVERA_000_320: After Gaius and I faced the Ruby Weapon, I had thought it to be all but indestructible. I'm glad to be proven wrong on this occasion.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SHADOWHUNTER_000_35: If Cid is as I remember him, it will not take long for him to finish investigating the remains of the Ruby Weapon. He never was one to waste time.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_351: My engineers are still in the field, but there's something I thought you should know right away.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_352: It's about the pilot. I'm not sure how to tell you this, but...
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SHADOWHUNTER_000_35: If Milisandia is dead, I only hope she was not made to suffer.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_354: Death would have been a kindness... In all my years, I've never seen such a perversion of science and nature.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_355: Her body was fused with the Ruby Weapon's core! Those last moments must have been spent in pure agony as her very life's essence was drained from her.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SHADOWHUNTER_000_35: So, she was sacrificed to power that infernal machine.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_VALDEAULIN_000_357: We must act quickly if we are to prevent the Empire from committing further atrocities. , is there any other information you can share with us regarding the Ruby Weapon prior to its...deactivation?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SHADOWHUNTER_000_35: Nael van Darnus? Did the legatus mean that much to Milisandia?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_359: From what I gather, it sounds as if data based on Nael's combat capabilities was used to override the pilot's consciousness after she was fused with the core.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_360: If this technology is perfected and the Empire begins implanting the memories of renowned warriors such as the White Raven into its soldiers, the Alliance won't stand a chance.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SHADOWHUNTER_000_36: Is such a thing even possible?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_A2_000_001: That's more or less how soul crystals work.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_A2_000_002: A similar method of transference was used on the prototype Estinien fought, was it not?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SHADOWHUNTER_000_36: Yes, it seems that such crystals are in common use throughout Eorzea. An ancient but effective means of passing on knowledge from one generation to the next.
Your friend did mention he overheard the signiferi loading various sets of data into the test model during the battle. It would appear that the system has been improved since then.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_365: While it may bear some similarities, we won't know for certain until we've analyzed the wreckage of the Ruby Weapon.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SHADOWHUNTER_000_36: It cannot be denied that combining combat data from an experienced soldier with the powers of an eikon has yielded remarkable results. But in doing so, the Empire has sunk to the very depths of depravity. This is beyond forgiveness.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_VALDEAULIN_000_367: For once, I agree with you. Yet one question remains unanswered: how were they able to obtain data on someone who was supposedly killed prior to the Calamity?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_CID_000_368: That's what I'm trying to determine. There is one possibility I'd like to explore, but I'll need to carry out a more thorough investigation first.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SHADOWHUNTER_000_36: Severa will provide support while you are in the field. Not only is she extremely well versed in the latest in Garlean technology, there are few soldiers I would rather have watching my back.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SHADOWHUNTER_000_37: In the meantime, Valdeaulin and I will follow the Ruby Weapon's tracks back to its point of origin.
We will learn what we can of the Weapon project and the manner in which Alfonse and the others are involved.
Should we uncover anything of value, we will relay it to the troops stationed here. For now, I suggest you use this lull in Garlean activity to recuperate.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_VALDEAULIN_000_373: Would I be correct in guessing that this belated reunion with those darling orphans of yours has stirred up memories of your time in Garlemald?
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_VALDEAULIN_100_374: If you so much as think of returning to your imperial masters, I will kill you.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SEVERA_000_375: If the cockpit remained intact, we may be able to glean information from the pilot.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_RESISTANCEOFFICER_0: So, you put down the Ruby Weapon? Gods, I wish I could've seen it! Not from too close, mind.
I suppose I should report news of your victory to the higher-ups. I realize you must've been through quite the ordeal, but could you give me a quick summary of the battle?

You make it sound so easy! From the way you tell it, anyone would think you slay hulking brutes like that for a living! I'll put all of this into a report, and leave a copy over there, should you fancy a bit of light reading.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_RESISTANCEOFFICER_1: Anyway, I expect you've got more pressing matters to take care of, like going for a celebratory pint. If the Garleans pluck up the courage to come knocking again, we'll let you know. Until then, rest up!
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_SYSTEM_000_403: Meanwhile, in the Werlyt magitek installation...
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALLIE_000_404: We should've told him the truth! He'd be able to help us, I know he would!
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALFONSE_000_405: That's exactly the problem, Allie. If he knew the true nature of the Weapon project, he'd find some way to interfere.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALFONSE_000_406: We've come too far to back down now. I won't let Milisandia's death be in vain.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALFONSE_000_407: Even if that means going against Father's wishes.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_REX_000_408: Cheer up, Alfonse. We can all go back to being one big happy family after we've dealt with those pesky Eorzeans. It'll be just like old times.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_RICON_000_409: If only it were that simple. There's no guarantee any of us'll make it back alive.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_REX_000_410: Excuse me? I think you're forgetting whose turn it is next, O ye of little faith! With me at the helm of the Sapphire Weapon, it'll be over before you know it.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_ALLIE_000_411: Whatever happens, Rex, promise you'll come back to us. I couldn't bear to lose you too.
TEXT_LUCKYW101_03783_WEAPONSGIENGINEER_0: Did you see that Weapon? Ah, of course you did, how silly of me! What I wouldn't give for the secrets of that armor plating!
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_DWARFMASTER03671_00: Lali-what a conveniently timed entrance-ho! I was just thinking that I ought to send someone to check on Anogg and Konogg.
They're still poking and prodding at those whatsits you dug up in the ruins. Which is all well and good until one of them sets off another explosion...
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_A1_000_001: Say no more. I wouldn't want anything to happen to the artifacts.
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_A1_000_002: Oh, I'm sure you'll notice if they blow up anything important.
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_DWARFMASTER03671_00: Thank you. You know how they get when they're curious about something.
By which point it'll be too late!
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_DWARFMASTER03671_10: Not to mention that our annual carnival is fast approaching. There's plenty that wants doing before we're ready, and I need those two to start pulling their weight.
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_DWARFMASTER03671_00: While you're looking in on them, remind them they've got duties outside of tinkering with rusty thingamabobs, will you? Maybe they'll listen if it's you doing the nagging.
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_DWARFMASTER03671_10: They seem to respect you─much as they respect anyone. Must be all the violence.
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_DWARFMASTER03671_00: You'll find them in the tunnels, of course. Can't lure them out of there for love nor money─and believe me, I've tried.
Don't like to leave those two unsupervised when I can help it, but I've got my hands full as it is.
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_KONOGG_000_050: Maybe it's supposed to do that...?
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_ANOGG_000_070: Ah, there you are. Can you believe this!?
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_ANOGG_000_071: I waited through days of “processing,” broke multiple tools, and after all of that...
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_ANOGG_000_072: Ugh. Ugh! Stupid son of a hob-swiving...
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_KONOGG_000_073: Anogg, not everyone is privy to your inner thoughts. Allow me to explain.
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_KONOGG_100_074: The pod confirmed that this device grants the user access to some sort of weaponry, which presumably means that it is indeed the key of which 2P spoke.
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_KONOGG_000_074: Unfortunately, no sooner had we gotten it working than it stopped again. Based on our previous experiences, we assume that it's run out of power, and will require a supplementary energy source.
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_ANOGG_000_075: So let's hurry up and find one! The sooner we get the key working, the sooner we can pulverize our enemies.
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_KONOGG_000_076: Now, wait just a moment. We aren't even certain what sort of weaponry is involved here. Even if we get the key working again, we shouldn't activate it willy-nilly.
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_ANOGG_000_077: Honestly, Konogg. This ceaseless whining of yours is why we never make any progress!
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_KONOGG_000_078: It's not whining, it's being ethical and prudent!
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_A2_000_001: Must you two always bicker so?
TEXT_LUCKTA201_03784_A2_000_002: Shall the victor be the first to draw blood, or the last man standing?
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_ANOGG_000_011: I agree that we still know too little about the machine lifeforms and androids. But that's precisely why we need to seize this opportunity!
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_ANOGG_000_012: If we claim the weaponry for ourselves, we'll know exactly what the enemy's capabilities are. Then─and only then─can we protect the village from comparable technology.
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_KONOGG_000_013: Fine, fine. I see your point. We'll be safer in the long run if we activate the weaponry sooner rather than later. Or everyone else will─I'll probably have dropped dead from trying to keep up with you.
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_ANOGG_000_014: Hahaha! You say that, but you're far too stubborn to die. That's why I can always count on you!
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_ANOGG_000_015: You too, most loyal and lethal assistant! Come along─we have a power source to find.
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_KONOGG_000_050: I'm never sure if Anogg has the better argument, or if she's just better at arguing. I guess it doesn't matter─she usually gets what she wants in the end.
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_ANOGG_000_061: I've been considering what we need in order to power the key─a hefty chunk of crystal from a knocker ought to do it, though I haven't quite worked out how we'll divert its energy for our purposes.
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_ANOGG_000_062: Konogg and I will think on it while you head over to the hollows and liberate that crystal. Find us when you're back in Komra.
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_KONOGG_000_150: And another thing─why does Anogg's way always have to be so fun...
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_ANOGG_000_161: Perfect. Now we can run some tests.
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_ANOGG_000_162: Yes, yes─it'll take a bit of experimentation to get the key powered up. It is science, you know.
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_ANOGG_000_163: Don't you worry, though─we'll have this thing in working order before you know it. While you wait, why not take some time for yourself? Have a nap, try some of our local delicacies, tell the chief to go bugger himself...
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_DWARFMASTER03671_00: Ah, and here's . I knew you had roped  into your schemes again.
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_ANOGG_000_166: They're good schemes! And anyway, you're the one who keeps sending  to check on us.
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_DWARFMASTER03671_00: I wouldn't have to if you'd do the work you were assigned. The carnival won't wait on your pet projects!
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_ANOGG_000_168: Fine, fine! Come on, Konogg. Let's get this over with.
TEXT_LUCKTA210_03785_DWARFMASTER03671_00: Frustrating as they are, you have to admire their enthusiasm for tinkering. If they can put even a tenth of that energy toward the carnival, we'll be ready in no time.

I hope you'll be able to attend. You won't have seen the like before, I assure you. Not to mention that we're eager to show our appreciation for your helping us with those machines─and there's no better way to do that than with a dwarven toast to your health or two. Dozen.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_YALFORT_000_000: Ah, there you are. I'm part of the team helping with the Ede─I mean, “highly classified and very, very secret...thing.”
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_YALFORT_000_001: The fact of the matter is, I've come to inform you of a rather interesting development. It's about the girl who was brought back from the Empty. She's finally woken up, you see.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_100_002: We heard the news from Thancred. Is it true?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_YALFORT_100_002: Why yes, it most certainly is!
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_YALFORT_210_002: Apparently, her name is Gaia. She claims to be a free citizen of Eulmore, although she remembers nothing of the events leading up to her attack on Eden.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_YALFORT_230_002: Parts of it, at the very least. We also cannot be sure whether she's telling the truth or if it's merely a ruse. She's yet to display any hostility, which is encouraging, I suppose.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_240_002: And Thancred's with her now, is he?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_YALFORT_250_002: Yes. He's taken her to Eulmore, mainly to verify what she's told us so far. Quiz the locals, that sort of thing.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_YALFORT_260_002: After that, the plan is to come back here, though they're taking rather longer than I'd anticipated. I do hope nothing is amiss...
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_003: (-???-)Good grief! Are you always this slow!?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_004: (-???-)At this rate, it'll be dark again before we know it! The night sky returning is all well and good, but it does make each day seem awfully short. And are you still dragging your heels back there!? At least act as if you've got a purpose, would you?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_005: Now look here, I'm not one of your servants. Why don't you try carrying your own luggage for a change?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_007: You lot are a sight for sore eyes. Yes, even you, Urianger. Gaia and I have just finished shipping her personal effects from Eulmore.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_009: I'm glad we could finally meet. Properly, I mean.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_100_009: So, ah... Did you learn anything useful?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_010: Other than where she lives, not an awful lot. Her supposed neighbors barely knew the first thing about her.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_011: Hells, she barely knows the first thing about herself. Her recollection of her life in Eulmore is patchy at best.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_012: But she seems convinced that she'll regain her memory if she accompanies us, and so she invited herself to join our merry band. And for her first act, she ordered me to carry her luggage.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_100_012: If you insist on standing around talking, might I suggest finding a place to sit down first? My feet are killing me.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_200_012: Then perhaps you should've chosen more sensible footwear. Still, it's not such a bad idea. Shall we?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_300_012: I've got so many things I want to ask, but I probably shouldn't bombard her with questions.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_310_012: Well, I've given you my early impression of Gaia, but I would be interested in hearing your opinion. Go on and talk to her and see what you make of her situation.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_320_012: Amnesia... 'Tis troubling though not entirely unexpected.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_YALFORT_330_012: That Gaia person appears to be none the worse off for her long sleep. A little surly, perhaps, but one can hardly expect her to be in the cheeriest of moods, given the circumstances.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_013: So you don't remember anything at all? Not attacking us, not falling unconscious?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_014: Such selective amnesia would rightly raise suspicion within those of a cautious mind.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_015: Yet if she doth speak the truth, it would lend credence to my current hypothesis, though admittedly some further─
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_016: Not now, Urianger, she's only just woken up. We don't want to bore her back to sleep.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_017: In any case, I prefer to follow my instincts, and they're telling me that Gaia means us no harm. After much deliberation, I thought it only right to let her know about our work in the Empty, as a sign of goodwill. After all, trust works both ways.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_100_017: Though, I would ask you, , not to let your guard down just yet.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_019: So you're the one I'm supposed to have fought? Come to think of it, I recognize you from somewhere.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_A1_000_001: Maybe I just have one of those faces.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_A1_000_002: So you should, considering you tried to kill me.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_020: Or perhaps you just didn't make much of an impression? But to be honest, I do feel that since meeting you, those hazy memories are becoming slightly clearer.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_022: Well, if Thancred's version of events is anything to go by, you weren't exactly holding back yourself. Still, it seems I didn't give you much of a choice but to defend yourself, so let's call it even. Not that I have any recollection of it...
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_024: ...It's like remembering fragments of a dream, only to realize those things actually happened. <sigh> It's as though my whole life has been leading to this...
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_026: Thou speakest as though thou didst expect these events.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_027: I guess you could say that. It's what the faerie tells me.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_030: I can't see it, but it's as though there's someone else inside me. And I can hear its voice in my head.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_031: It whispers to me and lets me use its power. “Magic,” I suppose you could call it, not that I know much about that sort of thing.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_032: And this power alloweth thee to tear open the fabric betwixt realities, that thou mayest call forth the aether-starved denizens of what remaineth of the Thirteenth?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_033: What!? Was that supposed to mean something or are you just spouting random words at me?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_034: Honestly, I don't know how you all put up with this. I've only just met him and his insufferable prattle is already giving me a headache!
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_100_034: Gods, I still can't believe I'm having this conversation. And to think that I was flying about in a suit of armor, waving a sword. That doesn't sound like me at all.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_038: Aye, the similarities cannot be ignored. Though it is too early to say with certainty, Gaia may well be the Oracle of Darkness.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_039: The Oracle...of Darkness? What does this mean?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_040: It means that you may have been right when you said she has something in common with Emet-Selch.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_041: Those who have been used as a living host by an Ascian have no recollection of events that occurred during their possession. This I know from personal experience.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_042: But Gaia seems to have some memories still, even if they're a little hazy. Moreover, she has remained in control of herself even when she heard the voice within. Much like you and Minfilia.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_045: And though Ryne was very much her own person, Minfilia's presence did exert a change upon her outward appearance, granting her hair and eyes a hue akin to that of our dear departed friend.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_046: It is therefore not unthinkable that Gaia's raven locks may be a manifestation of the Darkness which hath come to reside within her.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_047: But I was born like this. And my parents, they both had black hair, too.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_048: Or at least I think they did. It's been so long since I saw them, I can't remember too well...
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_050: But enough about me. You're Minfilia, aren't you? The Oracle of Light, who they were hosting in Eulmore?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_051: That's right, though imprisoning is a better word. They kept me locked away, and I didn't know much about Eulmore and its people, or the rest of the world for that matter.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_052: I see. And how exactly did the Oracle of Light come to run with the Warrior of Darkness?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_054: Yes, I still remember the day everyone went raving mad and Lord Vauthry fled. Everything after that is still a blur, though.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_056: From what Gaia's told me, she wasn't part of the mob that attacked us. But how was she able to resist Vauthry's control?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_057: Mayhap 'twas the intervention of this “faerie” of whom she speaketh.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_058: Hmm. As curious as that may be, we still don't know why she appeared out of nowhere as soon as Eden took flight.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_100_058: This is just a guess, but I'd say that the faerie reacted to it in some way, and for whatever reason, made me go after it.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_110_058: Yes, that seems like the only explanation.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_061: I don't know about you lot, but I've had enough nattering. I'm going back to Eden.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_063: The faerie wanted something from Eden, and knowing what that is will bring me a step closer to discovering exactly what has been living in my head all these years.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_068: Besides, my memories aren't going to restore themselves, and certainly not through idle chitchat. So I'm going, and that's that!
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_070: Insufferable. Utterly insufferable, and yet we can't well leave her to her own devices. Come on!
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_YALFORT_000_080: Was there some sort of disagreement with Miss Gaia?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_100_080: She can't have gone far, especially not in those heels...
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_100: I'm not entirely sure what I just witnessed, but I'm glad she's unharmed.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_101: Powers befitting the Oracle of Darkness...
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_102: When you fought Gaia, she opened voidgates, yes?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_103: Back in the Source, portals such as those were all too common, but tearing open the veil between the First and the Thirteenth is a different matter entirely.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_104: We should be thankful that she's not of a mind to turn that power against us. For now.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_105: A most fascinating application of aetherial manipulation. The destructive blast did manifest a significant span of time after the initial casting. With sufficient mastery of such a technique, a second spell could be made to smite the target at precisely the same moment.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_106: While it would demand exceptional aetherial control, its tactical potential cannot be denied.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_110: What are you all gawping at?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_111: I don't mean to stare, but it's not every day I see magic like that. So, this is the power of the faerie you spoke of?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_112: Ever since I was a child, it has whispered to me, telling me what to do. That's how I came to use its power.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_100_112: But there are things I can't even explain... Holes ripped in thin air, terrifying creatures crawling out, ghastly-looking blades and armor appearing out of nowhere. But worst of all is the dark energy that comes from inside.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_113: This power...it feels as though it's only flowing through me, and never truly mine. And even when it answers my call, it always takes a few moments for the spells to work.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_114: So in summary, you don't have control over the magic.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_115: Well, it's not as if I ever tried to control it. I haven't made a habit of fighting wild beasts.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_116: Unfortunately, it's part and parcel of traveling through Amh Araeng. And while I understand that you want answers, you're not going to find them unprepared as you are. But if your heart is set on this, then we'll help you.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_117: Ryne, think about what you're saying. You're seriously considering taking Gaia to see Eden?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_119: There's no telling what might happen if she loses control again, so the safest option is for her to stay away until our work is done. Somewhere we can keep an eye on her. You must realize, it's for her own good.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_120: I must concur with Thancred's assessment. At present, we know precious little of Gaia's origin and less still of her powers.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_121: If she is indeed the Oracle of Darkness, her presence may complicate a task already fraught with peril, placing our mission and her own well-being in jeopardy. In full knowledge of the risks, dost thou still wish to pursue this course?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_123: It wasn't so long ago that I was living in isolation, being held against my will. Maybe the people keeping an eye on me thought that was for my own good, too.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_124: But if we shut Gaia away for our own convenience, we're no better than Vauthry and Ran'jit!
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_125: I've learned that when someone is in need, we must reach out a helping hand, not push them away. Now, it's my turn. To do for Gaia what you've all done for me.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_100_125: Even knowing the danger that lies ahead, I won't choose the easy way out. This is the path I've chosen!
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_126: Is that good enough for you?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_100_128: Well, can't say fairer than that. How about you, Urianger?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_110_128: The light of thy spirit doth burn bright.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_130: Mine apologies, my dear, but we felt it necessary to test thy resolve. Let it suffice it to say thou hast left no room for doubt.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_132: For what it's worth, Ryne, I never doubted you. But make no mistake, the danger that Urianger and I spoke of is all too real. If you're prepared to go through with this, we'll be right there beside you.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_133: That means a lot to me. Thank you.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_135: I couldn't care less who I travel with, but if we're going to go, then let's get going already. There's supposed to be some sort of craft waiting at the southern watchtower, yes? Come along then, and don't fall behind.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_140: Of course I'm worried about what may happen when Gaia gets close to Eden. We'll keep a close eye on her, make sure she's all right.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_141: Though our circumstance hath changed, our mission most assuredly hath not. Restoring life to the Empty remaineth our primary objective.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_142: Why couldn't you leave this craft in Mord Souq instead of all the way out here? <sigh> Actually, don't bother explaining. Whatever the reason is, I'm sure it's something frightfully uninteresting. Let's be about it, shall we?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_150: It might be a bit of a tight squeeze with the five of us, but we'll manage. Perhaps Urianger can sit on top of our luggage?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_RYNE_000_160: Everything seems fine here, as far as I can tell. As for Gaia, she hasn't started attacking anything yet, so I'll take that as a good sign.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_THANCRED_000_161: As usual, we should keep our sojourn here as brief as possible. Let's tend to business quickly.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_URIANGER_000_162: I had hoped that, during our absence, the rebalancing of ambient aether might work further change. Alas, 'twas not to be...
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_170: Eden... Where I'll find the answers I seek.
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_171: The bringer of the Flood, the first sin eater. Would it lead me to my past, or my future?
TEXT_LUCKRA201_03787_GAIA_000_172: What awaited on the path ahead, I couldn't say. But I had no choice but to take the first step...
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_000: Everything seems fine here, as far as I can tell. As for Gaia, she hasn't started attacking anything yet, so I'll take that as a good sign.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_001: As usual, we should keep our sojourn here as brief as possible. Let's tend to business quickly.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_URIANGER_000_002: I had hoped that, during our absence, the rebalancing of ambient aether might work further change. Alas, 'twas not to be...
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_010: I know what it's like. It was the same for me.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_011: But I was lucky, because Thancred freed me from Eulmore, and I had a chance to see the world. More importantly, though, I met all kinds of people, and they taught me not to live in another's shadow, but to be myself.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_012: Maybe one day, you'll have that chance, too.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_015: "One day“? What's that supposed to mean!?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_017: I don't know how the great Oracle of Light sees such things...
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_018: But for someone like me, who's only known life in Eulmore, there was no tomorrow. There was no future. Only the here and now.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_019: And while we waste time on these meaningless conversations, I feel each moment of my life slipping away. Time... It won't wait. Not for me, not for anyone.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_020: I don't know how much longer I can hold on...to who I am.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_022: Gaia? Hmph. That's probably not even my real name.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_024: When Thancred asked me my name, I couldn't remember.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_025: That's when the faerie whispered to me. “Gaia...”
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_026: But if you grew up in Eulmore, surely someone there must know who you are?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_028: Everyone I once knew had either disappeared or had been turned into sin eaters. Those whose faces and names I still remember, that is. In the end, we found not a single person who so much as recognized me.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_029: As far as I can recall, I've never been the most sociable person, but still...
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_030: Well, even if it's not your real name, I think “Gaia” sounds lovely. If you're happy with it, then that's what I'll call you.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_031: And if you're willing, instead of the Oracle of Light, please call me Ryne. It's not the name I was born with─that's long forgotten now─but the one the people whom I consider family gave to me.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_033: Well, as much as I'd love to keep up this chatting, there's something that's bothering me. I thought the faerie would've reacted to Eden in some way, but so far, nothing whatsoever.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_034: From what I gather, it wasn't until Eden started moving that I appeared out of the blue.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_035: Perhaps if you were to actually try flying it somewhere, the faerie might break its silence. If you've got elements to restore, or whatever it was, why don't you hurry up and get it over with?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_A1_000_002: You need to learn some manners.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_036: Aye, it may be best to resign ourselves to her mannerisms. A good thing we're not wholly unfamiliar with attending nobility, given certain company in the Scions.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_URIANGER_000_037: Of whomsoever dost thou speak, I wonder?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_038: And you need to stop wasting my time!
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_039: All right, everyone, I think we've talked for long enough. If you're ready, let's make our way to Eden!
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_040: I've done some reading about the lands swallowed up by the Flood, but it's no easy task to find locations with a dominant element.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_041: I'm glad we have Urianger to point us in the right direction.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_042: Ryne's little chat with Gaia reminded me that, for all our obvious differences, there are things we have in common. I, too, grew up not knowing who my parents were. The day Louisoix gave me the surname “Waters” was one I'll never forget.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_043: Years later, it was under rather more desperate circumstances that I gave a certain young girl the name “Minfilia.”
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_044: Little did I know then that it would end up crossing time and space, taking on a meaning I could never have foreseen. It came to be passed on to one girl after another, binding them to a fate not their own.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_045: In a sense, it may be said that I chose not only one, but two names for Ryne. But by whatever name she is called, she is truly her own person now.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_046: And as central to our lives as names are, I believe that it isn't the name itself, but the bonds it symbolizes that matter most.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_047: My memories...I think they're slowly coming back to me.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_048: My mother and father would constantly blather on about how the Flood of Light could return to end the world when we least expect it, and that we should live each day as though it were our last.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_049: They would often say, “I wish this moment would last forever!”
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_050: That was until they were selected for ascension by Lord Vauthry and were never to be seen again. Since I had no other relatives, or even any close friends to speak of, I was left alone in the world.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_051: <sigh> A past like that hardly seems worth remembering, does it?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_URIANGER_000_060: Following the initial changes wrought by the release of water and earth, the Empty hath displayed no further signs of alteration.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_URIANGER_000_061: Stability, some may call this and be satisfied, but in truth it is passivity. A passivity stemming from Light's ever-pervasive presence.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_URIANGER_000_062: If we are to break the status quo, we must needs employ a catalyst─a third element that shall rouse and stabilize those unleashed energies in activity.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_064: So the primal would be...Ramuh, yes? From what I've heard, he's a guardian of the forest and not particularly keen on conflict. But you've actually fought him, haven't you?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_A2_000_001: He's half-man, half-beard, and another half-beard for good measure.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_A2_000_002: I spent most of the time chasing after orbs, with varying degrees of success.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_065: Ah, yes. Thancred mentioned that he more closely resembles a person than a beast, unlike most other primals. And apparently he tends not to move about much.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_066: I wonder if the sylphs had anything to do with that? I hear they can be quite mischievous, much like the pixies of Il Mheg.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_067: I'm glad to see our lessons have paid off.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_068: Well, it's like you say. If we want to call forth an accurate representation of the primal, I should picture it in my mind as clearly as possible. At the very least, it's worth a try. But the rest is up to .
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_069: In order for this to work, we need to actually fly somewhere, yes? So rather than sitting in one spot while you exchange anecdotes, why don't you get this blasted thing moving first?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_URIANGER_000_070: One must admit, the suggestion is not without merit. Ryne, might I suggest the Gandof Thunder Plains as our next location?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_URIANGER_000_071: These plains, it is writ, were perpetually blanketed in storm clouds, the only source of illumination the ceaseless barrage of lightning. The ambient aether that lingereth there shall provide ideal conditions for the summoning.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_072: Then that's where we're heading. Come on, Eden, we've got a job to do!
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_073: This should be as good a spot as any.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_SYSTEM_000_075: Memories of Ramuh flash through your mind...
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_080: All the lightning that's fallen here over the years has left the ground covered in craters. But don't worry, Eden will give you something more even to stand on.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_081: Even if Ryne has done a good job of memorizing my description of Ramuh, it will likely make little difference to how he manifests. After all, it's your memories that shape the summoning, not hers.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_URIANGER_000_082: The area is saturated with lightning-aspected aether, this I am able to confirm. In addition to the primal, be thou wary of stray bolts that may occur as a result of our activity.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_083: I don't think I've ever been anywhere like this before. And I'm not sure I'd want to come back. Too dreary for my liking.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_084: Would be nice if our next destination is a little cheerier, but I suppose I can't exactly choose if I want answers.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_090: I had my eye on Gaia the entire time you were fighting Ramuh, and besides the sort of reaction you might expect from someone watching you take on a half-man, half-flying-horse thunder god, I didn't notice anything out of the ordinary.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_091: The fact that Eden itself also showed no signs of being affected by her presence can only be a good thing. But I'd understand if Gaia herself were more than a little disappointed that she's no closer to the answers she seeks.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_URIANGER_000_092: Once again, 'twas a most superlative display of thy puissance. Now, I could not fail but notice─that body did belong to Ixion, fabled equine embodiment of lightning. Hast thou perchance encountered the beast?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_093: So that...thing was created based on your memories? Maybe there's a way we can use Eden to summon the faerie like that...
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_100: I thought I was prepared to expect anything, but I didn't expect Ramuh to turn out quite like that.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_101: Appearance aside, he was quite aggressive as well. The sylph's belief in him as a kindly guardian clearly makes a difference to his temperament.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_102: Anyway, I'm just glad it's over. Let's get back to the camp and see if anything's changed!
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_110: Hmm... The crystal's a different color, but apart from that, it all looks the same.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_111: It may look the same, aye, but it feels different. The air has grown slightly more humid, as it does before rain.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_112: I have to say, I'm not exactly prepared for wet weather. If Eden can control elements and so on, can't you tell it to send those clouds somewhere else?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_113: Speaking of which, I'm not very impressed with its so-called powers. If changing yellow crystals to purple is the extent of its abilities, it's no surprise the faerie didn't bother showing up. I hope that whatever's next is more worthwhile.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_URIANGER_000_114: Rather than influencing the ground beneath our feet, Eden hath brought change to the firmament above.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_URIANGER_000_115: And yet 'tis clear that a more dynamic element is required for the natural cycle of precipitation and evaporation to be complete.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RYNE_000_116: So we need movement... Would wind do the trick?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_THANCRED_000_118: It seems we have a plan. Let's not dwell too much on the effects of each individual element, and instead focus on seeing them all restored.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_119: The power of an Oracle... Not to be sniffed at, it seems.
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_120: All my life, you were a constant companion, your voice ever seeping into my mind. Why then, of all times, did you abandon me?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_GAIA_000_121: Deaf even to the crashing of thunder... Or were you simply biding your time?
TEXT_LUCKRA202_03788_RAMUH_000_130: I have taken thy measure, Bringer of Light.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_000: As much as I bemoan Urianger's long-winded explanations, we'd be lost without him to take care of all the aetherial science and whatnot. Obviously, I'm quite sparing with my praise, as I wouldn't want it to go to his head.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_001: I'm not sure what I was expecting to see after restoring the lightning element, but I did feel a little disheartened. Still, as Thancred and Urianger say, there are changes taking place, even if they're not immediately obvious.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_002: One plan fails to achieve the desired effect, so you move on to the next with minimal brooding and prattling. It seems we're finally learning.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_010: Ere we set out once more, might I ask if thou art familiar with the process by which rain is made to fall?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_A1_000_003: We scholars tend to have a fairly solid grasp of it, yes.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_011: Then thou shan't have difficulty understanding the explanation to come.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_012: Hmm... It certainly would not be beyond the Allagans to manipulate the weather, if such is thy suggestion, but it is of naturally occurring phenomena that I would speak.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_013: Ah, I spoke without regard for thy profession. I daresay thou art better versed in such matters than I. Might I impose on thee to divulge the intricacies to the less informed members of our party?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_014: Then, with thy permission, I shall proceed.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_015: With the restoration of our first element, the Empty was once more blessed with the most essential ingredient in the cycle of precipitation: water.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_016: Under normal circumstances, the heat existent in the atmosphere would cause water to evaporate from the land's surface.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_017: As invisible vapor, it is borne by the wind high unto the firmament, where it doth condense as clouds before descending once more, returning to the land in the form of rain.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_018: It seems we need wind-aspected aether to create more clouds. That it hasn't rained yet must mean there aren't enough.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_019: And even before that, we need fire-aspected aether to make the water evaporate.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_020: It seems to me that one's not much good without the other. Why don't you just draw out both elements together?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_021: You're suggesting that  fight two deiform entities, each one as deadly as Ramuh, at the same time? Do you realize how absurd that is?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_022: And yet...'tis a notion that doth warrant further consideration.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_024: Cast your minds, if you will, to the elemental wheel I did show to you in the Bookman's Shelves.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_025: Wind giveth rise to lightning, whose spark doth produce fire. By restoring both wind and fire in tandem, we may maintain balance between these dynamic elemental forces.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_026: The ensuing battle shall indubitably present an ordeal unlike any  hath ever faced. I believe, however, that this path doth lead to the prize we seek.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_027: Oh, so perhaps it's not so absurd after all, eh, Thancred?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_028: I wouldn't dream of questioning Urianger's grasp of the science behind it. My concern is for the burden this would place not only on , but Ryne as well.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_029: What do you both make of the plan?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_030: If Urianger thinks it'll work, I'm willing to give it a try!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_031: As long as you know what you're letting yourselves in for. You're going to need all your strength, so see that you get plenty of rest.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_040: I'd rather Ryne keep her mind on our work here than worry about Gaia. Mind you, it might be better for them to clear the air before we go any further.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_041: I have selected a location in which wind- and fire-aspected aether lie dormant, though I shall wait until Ryne hath completed her preparations ere I dispense with the particulars.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_042: I can't stand all of this waiting around. Having grown up in Eulmore, I'm used to only living for the moment.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_043: We never had any reason to concern ourselves with “later,” “tomorrow,” “the future,” and so on. Those things simply didn't matter.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_044: But after Lord Vauthry disappeared and the night returned, everyone in Eulmore started thinking differently. I was only there for a short time with Thancred, and I couldn't believe how much it had changed.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_045: It was almost as though under Lord Vauthry's rule, time had stopped moving altogether, and when it ended, life went back to how it was supposed to have been. They realized they had their whole lives ahead of them, to make plans, and look forward to a new day.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_046: It feels like I'm the only one who can't move on, as if I'm still stuck in the past. What's worse, I can barely remember any of it. Even so, I can't stand the way they act as if the past never happened, choosing to forget it all.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_SYSTEM_000_051: It seems Ryne is reluctant to air her concerns. Were you to rally her spirits, she may become more willing to talk.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_060: Yes, you're right. There's no use in trying to pilot Eden while I've got other things on my mind.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_062: The truth is, that apart from Alisaie and Alphinaud, I hardly know anyone my own age. I thought that I should make an effort to be nice to Gaia, but... Well, you've seen how she is around me.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_063: I understand that she's got her own problems to deal with, but I thought that maybe I could help her in some way.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_064: It's not my place to intrude, and I should probably just leave her be until we've finished restoring the elements. After all, that's more important, isn't it?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_065: Let me talk to Gaia while you concentrate on the task at hand.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_066: ...Is what I would've said, once upon a time.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_067: It seems to me that you're the one best qualified to take care of this little problem. I know she can be a bit prickly─to put it mildly─but if anyone can get through to her, it's you.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_068: Although we've only known her for a short while, we're all she's got, and I think she realizes that. Just let her know she's not alone and she'll come around eventually.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_069: All right, I'll give it a try. Umm... Do you have any advice?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_A2_000_001: Thancred certainly has the gift of the gab. He'll know what to say.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_A2_000_002: Urianger can talk the hind legs off a behemoth. Why not ask him?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_070: I'm afraid that since arriving in the First, I've had little time to mingle with any of the locals, and I haven't a clue what young women like Gaia would be interested in.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_071: Ah, that's given me an idea! I'll start with some small talk and go from there!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_072: Actually, since before she even woke up, I've been asking Lyna about what's popular in the Crystarium. I thought it might be nice to show Gaia around the place one day, you see...
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_073: Though I am proficient in many tongues, such as Fae, I cannot claim to be as well versed in the parlance of the younger generation. Their predilections and inclinations are a mystery I have yet to unravel.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_074: I don't know much about it either...but I believe I have a plan!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_075: Before she even woke up, I've been asking Lyna about what's popular in the Crystarium. I thought it might be nice to show Gaia around the place one day, you see...
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_076: So that's what you were doing? I suppose it makes for a nice change of pace from all that studying.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_077: And I must commend thee on thy choice of confidant. The captain's powers of observation maketh her a veritable font of wisdom concerning the behavior of the Crystarium's citizenry.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_078: Yes, and now it's time to put that knowledge to good use.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_079: Don't let the fear of rejection hold you back. Persistence is the key.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_080: Speaking from experience, by any chance?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_082: Lessons learned from days spent in pursuit of ladies fair, one might suspect.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_083: Gah! You couldn't help yourself, could you!?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_084: It's all right, Thancred. Your secret's safe with me!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_085: Ahem! May I remind you that the reason we're here is to create a better future for everyone in the First, which includes you and Gaia.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_086: While it might not be on the same scale as bringing life back to the Empty, if you're able to befriend her, that will be another way of contributing to a brighter tomorrow.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_087: So go on, she's waiting for you.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_SYSTEM_000_089: Ryne is ready to approach the decidedly unapproachable Gaia. You had best observe the conversation from within earshot.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_090: Hmm... She looks like she's got a lot on her mind. Maybe now's not such a good time?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_SYSTEM_000_091: Ryne is ready to approach the decidedly unapproachable Gaia. You had best observe the conversation from within earshot.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_092: It's when Ryne and I face our problems together that it truly feels like we're family. Or at least, what I imagine it would be like. I suppose we both grew up without our birth parents to guide us, but I think we turned out rather well given the circumstances.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_093: I wonder if this is the kind of bond that F'lhaminn shared with Minfilia...
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_094: Thancred may have taken on the role of Ryne's surrogate father, but I have of late become something of a mentor to her, though largely in instilling what knowledge I can of the aetherial sciences. A more attentive student thou shalt seldom find.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_095: Instead of bothering me when I'm obviously not in the mood to talk, why don't you get back to work?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_102: Oh! Ah, nothing really. It can wait till later...
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_103: For all we know, there might not even be a “later.”
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_104: If you've got something to say, hurry up and spit it out.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_105: Erm... Is everything all right? Not feeling strange from being around Eden or anything?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_106: Is that what you came here to talk about?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_107: Actually... I wanted to ask you...
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_108: W-Would you like to go and have coffee biscuits with me?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_110: Coffee biscuits! They serve them at the Second Serving in the Crystarium. Everyone's talking about them, so I thought that maybe once we've finished our work here, you and I could go there together.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_111: Let me get this straight. You came to talk to me about biscuits?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_112: Yes! They're light and crispy and when you dip them in the coffee they go all nice and squidgy!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_113: The only reason you're even interested in that in the first place is because everyone else is doing it. Can't you think for yourself?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_114: I do what I want, when I want. After all, the world could end at any moment.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_115: That's not going to happen! Not if I've got anything to do with it!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_116: Listen, Gaia. I understand what you're going through. Believe me, I do. But you mustn't lose hope! A new day will come. Then another, and another. Life's not so bad if you give it a chance, you'll see!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_117: Shut up! You think you know me!? Even I don't know who I am!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_118: Until I find the truth, I'll never be free.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_120: I've seen enough pain, enough loss, and I don't want to see any more! And that includes you, Gaia!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_121: Why do you care so much about other people? What have they ever done for you? I'm sure you haven't forgotten how we Eulmorans treated you, the precious Oracle of Light. Like a bird in a cage!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_122: And yet, you act as if none of that ever happened. So forgiving, so selfless.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_123: You and your family brought back the night sky, and you finally had the chance to lead a normal life. But instead, you're flying around in a giant sin eater, trying to turn a barren wasteland into some sort of paradise, and for what?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_124: I may not remember much of my past, but I'm fairly certain I've never heard of anything so ridiculous. Out of morbid curiosity, I'll see it through to the end, but if you think that makes us friends, you are very much mistaken.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_126: I surmise that to keep Gaia waiting overlong would only agitate her further.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_130: I think we've both rested for long enough. Let's get started, shall we?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_131: <sigh> I hope it all goes according to plan...
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_132: Ryne's looking a bit down in the doldrums, but you let me worry about that. We can't allow anything to interfere with whatever goes on in your mind when summoning those primals.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_133: Not you as well? Look, I've had enough small talk to last me a lifetime, so don't even bother. I believe you have a job to do, yes? Then be quick about it.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_140: To defeat the deiform manifestations of both wind and fire shall require every last mote of thy strength. That thou hast triumphed over such beings in previous encounters should be at the forefront of thy mind as we commence the summoning.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_141: Where are we going this time, Urianger?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_142: The place called Ashfall doth satisfy our requirements, I believe. The fables speak of travelers sweltering beneath the blazing heat of the midday sun, while after nightfall, slicing winds did tear at their cloaks.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_143: Hmm... I see. Hopefully it won't be quite that bad when I draw out the elements.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_144: Ryne, my dear. May I remind thee that to focus is not the same as to deny other thoughts. Whatsoever it is that troubleth thee, thou wouldst be better for acknowledging it.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_145: Yes, you're right, of course... It's Gaia that I'm worried about.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_146: That is well. May thy concern for her lend thee yet more strength.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_147: It's time. I'll begin drawing out wind and fire in equal measure.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_148: , we'll only get one chance at this, so let's make it count!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_SYSTEM_000_149: Memories of Garuda and Ifrit rage through your mind...
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_150: If we summon two primals at once, maybe they'll fight each other? That way, you'll only need to beat the one left standing. But I suppose it defeats the purpose of it if you don't take them both down at the same time.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_151: How long has it been since our encounter with Ifrit and his Amalj'aa followers?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_152: My studies indicate that no equivalent of Garuda's servants, the Ixal, are present here on the First. My hypothesis as to the reason why can perhaps wait till another time.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_153: I wonder what sort of hellish beasts you've conjured up this time?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_THANCRED_000_160: Combining the contrasting powers of different primals... That seems an awful lot like the Ultima Weapon. In any case, I'm pleased to see that you were as successful here as you were at the Praetorium.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_161: That two such ferocious beings should meld into a single entity is frightful indeed. Further research must needs be performed to fully comprehend this unexpected phenomenon.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_162: For a moment, I thought Ryne had lost control of the aether. Luckily, we managed to avoid any major disasters, from what I can tell.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_170: That was incredible! I never imagined they would fuse together like that, but you took them down all the same.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_171: I suppose the main thing is that we're now two elements closer to restoring the aether of the Empty. Let's go and see what difference it's made!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_180: It actually worked! Just like Urianger said it would!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_URIANGER_000_182: Indeed, our endeavors have been repaid manifold.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_RYNE_000_183: I wonder what will happen when we restore ice?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_185: One more element, and then what?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_186: You'll have achieved the impossible, while I'll still be...nothing. No memory, no past, no family... Nothing.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_187: The world has moved on and left me behind. Anyone who ever knew me is either dead or gone.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_188: So, almighty Eden, you can mend this broken world, but you can't restore one girl's memories!?
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_189: Give me my life back, damn you!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIAVOICE_100_190: Extinguish the accursed Light... Awaken our true power...
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_191: Enough riddles! Tell me who I am!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIAVOICE_100_194: Reclaim your memories... Fulfill your destiny!
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_201: Amidst the sound of falling rain, your voice called from within.
TEXT_LUCKRA203_03789_GAIA_000_202: Long after the rain passed, your voice echoed on...
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_RYNE_000_000: Poor Gaia... If the faerie lives inside her, why would it let her suffer like this? I wish there was something we could do to help...
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_URIANGER_000_001: Pray be on thy guard, my friend. Gaia may yet relinquish control to the voice within...
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_002: Ungh... Just get it over with, would you?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_THANCRED_000_010: While this downpour is precisely the result we were hoping for, the novelty of standing outside in the rain does wear off rather quickly. Not to mention, Gaia's looking a bit under the weather. Let's continue this conversation in Eden's core.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_RYNE_000_020: Now that I think about it, I don't really know all that much about Eden.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_RYNE_000_021: Since we need to find out how it's connected to Gaia, I should try to understand it at a deeper level. To be honest, there isn't much else I can do...
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_THANCRED_000_022: I'm not sure what's going on with Gaia, but it's certainly a cause for concern. Perhaps this is the faerie making itself known...
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_023: What does it want? Why won't it tell me?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_URIANGER_000_030: Ere we set forth to restore the element of ice, I would discuss the manner in which the summoning shall be undertaken.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_031: Just tell me one thing: is this going to bring the Empty back to the way it was before the Flood?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_URIANGER_000_032: While none can say for certain, the change we have observed at points of aetherial intersection doth give us cause for optimism.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_URIANGER_000_033: It may be reasonably assumed that the Empty shall continue to transform and, in the decades to come, regain a semblance of its former state.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_THANCRED_000_035: I don't think you've quite grasped the sheer scale of the damage left in the wake of the Flood. It would've swallowed the entire world if Minfilia hadn't stopped it.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_THANCRED_000_036: Even if Ryne has inherited her blessing, wounds like that don't heal overnight. After all, the Empty has been utterly devoid of life for a hundred years.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_RYNE_000_037: And it might take even longer than that to bring life back. I don't expect immediate results, but I do know that it will stay like this forever unless we do something about it.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_URIANGER_000_038: My sentiments precisely. Only once the final element is restored shall we have a glimpse of the future that awaiteth those of generations yet to come.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_039: You'd do all this, for a world you may not live long enough to see? While here I am, so absorbed in my own problems that I spare barely a thought for anyone besides myself...
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_100_039: For so long, I've listened to that voice...telling me what to do, who to be. I was so scared of what might happen if I disobeyed. But I don't want to live like that anymore. I want to be...me.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_110_039: Who am I? What am I? Perhaps it's better if I never find out. If Ryne's the Oracle of Light, here to mend this broken world, what does that make me?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_120_039: Gaia, the Oracle of Darkness, bringer of misery and death! A monster. It's no wonder they left me. Mother, Father... And next, it'll be all of you. Then I'll be back where I started, where I've always been. Alone.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_100_040: What's wrong? Afraid I might lose control and ruin all your carefully laid plans!?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_RYNE_110_040: No! It's you I'm worried about!
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_041: Ryne, I... I'm going outside. To clear my head. You...just do what you need to do, all right?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_THANCRED_000_044: If we have a repeat of her first “visit” to Eden, we may even be joined by those voidsent friends of hers... If you go and see what Gaia's doing, Urianger and I will stay with Ryne.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_050: My name is Gaia... That's what you said, isn't it?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_051: Eden... The Flood... What does it all mean?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_052: No, it can't be... Is this what it's been waiting for all this time?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIAVOICE_090_054: The Darkness that dwells within you, Gaia.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIAVOICE_100_054:
The accursed spawn of Light are drawn to it, like moths to a flame.
Pathetic, mindless, and easily bent to my will...
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIAVOICE_100_055: Now, the time of awakening has come!
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_THANCRED_000_057: , Ryne senses sin eaters! What's happened?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_THANCRED_000_058: Don't try to fight them─just bring Gaia back inside. Quickly, now!
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_THANCRED_000_060: She's in a bad way, but at least she doesn't seem to have lost control.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_URIANGER_000_061: What entity is this that should hold a horde of sin eaters in its thrall? And to what end?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_THANCRED_000_071: That's a concern for later. First, we must deal with those sin eaters.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_URIANGER_000_072: , if thou wouldst care to repel our assailants without, I would task Thancred with standing guard within. I shall tend to Gaia meanwhile.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_RYNE_000_080: I'm not sure if there's much Eden can do to help, but I'll try to keep it steady.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_THANCRED_000_081: While Urianger watches over Gaia, I'll tend to any eaters that chance to slip inside.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_URIANGER_000_082: Whereas before, 'twas Gaia who sought to destroy Eden, on this occasion she hath become the target...
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_THANCRED_000_090: The interior is secure. With the eaters gone, I thought that Gaia might show some sign of improvement, but she hasn't so much as stirred.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_URIANGER_000_091: Sin eaters drawn to the Oracle of Darkness, just as she herself was drawn to Eden, first and foremost among their kind.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_RYNE_000_100: She won't wake up! What do we do?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_112: So, I'm all alone. Even the faerie is gone...
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_113: Endless silence, endless darkness... Is this what death feels like?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_114: It's no use. No one can hear me. How ironic... All those times I wanted peace and quiet, and now that I finally have it, I wish I had someone to talk to.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_115: I thought I couldn't stand to be around them. All their interfering and fussing... And yet, I was never lonely.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_116: But it's no use... Even after everything we went through, my memories still won't come back. There is no future awaiting me, only emptiness.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_117: Those memories...they can stay lost forever, if only this pain will leave me.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_118: Now, I close my eyes and sink into darkness...
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_100_118: And then I'll suffer no more.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_122: I understand now. Why wait for tomorrow to claim us?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_124: This perfect moment never has to end.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_RYNE_000_125: (-???-)I'm not giving up on you, Gaia! Say something!
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_RYNE_000_128: Remember all the things we said we'd do? Like going to the Second Serving for coffee biscuits!
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_131: I never agreed to anything of the sort.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_RYNE_000_132: Oh, thank goodness! I was so worried about you!
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_133: Ugh, do you have to be so loud?
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_134: The faerie fell silent, only to be replaced by Ryne's voice ringing through my head.
TEXT_LUCKRA204_03790_GAIA_000_135: I never thought I would be so glad to hear it.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_000: We still don't know exactly what happened, but at least the danger's passed for now.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_THANCRED_000_001: Whatever that thing was, it was able to control a vast swarm of sin eaters, much like Vauthry. Then again, it's clearly nothing like a Lightwarden... In any case, it's gone now. I just hope it stays gone.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_URIANGER_000_002: Though Gaia hath regained consciousness, I surmise that it shall be some time before she is fully recovered from her ordeal.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_GAIA_000_010: You've all gone through a lot of trouble on my part. For what it's worth, I'm sorry. Anyway, I've delayed you for long enough. Please, carry on with what you came to do.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_011: I'm glad you're back to your usual self, but how are you feeling?
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_GAIA_000_012: Much better now, but something is still bothering me. The faerie spoke to me in a dream, and a stream of memories rushed through my mind. I don't recall anything like this happening before, and I'm not sure what it all means.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_GAIA_000_014: I can't make any sense of them. They were only brief flashes, seen through someone else's eyes. At least, that's what it felt like.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_THANCRED_000_015: Minfilia─that is, the first Oracle of Light─once served Hydaelyn as the Word of the Mother.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_THANCRED_000_016: If the Oracle of Darkness is her counterpart under Zodiark, then we had best prepare ourselves for the worst.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_URIANGER_000_017: Aye, the night's return did tip the aetherial balance towards activity, which may have served to awaken the fragment of His power in the First.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_URIANGER_000_018: Having thus roused, He did then fix His gaze upon she who had been marked by Darkness─Gaia.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_019: Marked or no, Gaia's still her own person.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_GAIA_000_020: Anyway, let's forget about all that for now. There'll be plenty of time to think it through once the last element's restored.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_URIANGER_000_021: If thou believest thyself well enough, then I see no reason for delay. Let us forthwith attend to the revitalization of ice.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_THANCRED_000_022: Shiva, then. , as the only one here to have actually seen the primal, perhaps you could describe her for us?
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_A1_000_001: A woman named Ysayle made herself a vessel for Shiva.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_A1_000_002: She and the great wyrm Hraesvelgr shared an undying bond.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_023: So, she summoned into her body the imagined essence of someone who lived over a thousand years ago? That such a thing should be possible...
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_024: To find a kindred spirit in such an ancient and fearsome creature... I can hardly imagine what sort of a person she must've been.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_URIANGER_000_025: The long since departed Shiva was a source of great inspiration to Ysayle, whose method of summoning differed greatly from any we had previously encountered.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_URIANGER_000_026: By the Echo did she bear witness to the deeds of the noble Shiva, and thus was she moved to dedicate her being to that selfsame cause. 'Twas this devotion that granted her the power of a primal.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_027: So, she was able to control it herself...?
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_GAIA_000_028: Not getting any funny ideas, are you?
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_029: Ah, just thinking aloud, that's all! Anyway, we'd better get going.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_URIANGER_000_030: Our journey leadeth to a great glacier situated in the northernmost region of the Empty.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_031: I'll get us there as quickly as I can!
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_032: It's time to draw out the aether.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_034: ...That I should go with you this time. I want to be the vessel for Shiva!
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_035: Being still and passive by nature, ice is the element that is the most strongly aligned to Light. I'll need to get close and use my own abilities as well as Eden's to draw it out.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_URIANGER_000_036: So that the Oracle of Light becometh the Oracle of Ice...
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_URIANGER_000_037: I cannot claim to be in favor of this stratagem, and yet... The primal we encountered in the Source was summoned in much the same manner. The inherent advantages are undeniable─
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_THANCRED_000_039: Have you forgotten what  does to the primals we summon!? I'm not about to stand by and watch as  and Ryne beat the tar out of each other.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_THANCRED_000_040: In any case, the aether only returns to the Empty once the creature's been slain, although it seems you haven't taken that into consideration yet. Presumably, there's a safe way to disperse it, but it's still far too risky.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_THANCRED_000_041: ...I thought you had more sense, Ryne.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_042: But it's not as bad as it sounds!
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_URIANGER_000_043: Were the deiform entity as volatile as the primals we have previously summoned, 'twould be logical to assume that, in her role as conduit, Ryne would be hard-pressed to retain control.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_URIANGER_000_044: would have no recourse but to defend  by any means necessary, else  life be forfeit.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_045: I know it's dangerous, but I can't let that hold me back. Please, I've got to try!
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_THANCRED_000_046: But I don't see why this is even necessary in the first place. You never had to take risks like this for the other elements.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_047: Eden possesses almost infinite power, but what would happen if it began acting without my intervention?
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_048: If it started to feed on the aether, just like other sin eaters, it would undo all of our hard work!
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_URIANGER_100_048: 'Tis a disconcerting eventuality, and one which cannot be dismissed.
TEXT_LUCKRA205_03791_RYNE_000_049: I'm worried that even if we realign the elements, things will eventually return to how they were following the Flood.
